mutation_battery.note: Mutation (b) SURVIVED the first attempt and that is recorded rather than smoothed over. The correction-chain test used distinct created_at values, so it never exercised the comparator's tiebreak and `>` passed. The gap was in the test, not the implementation: a tie-ordering test was added, asserting both page orders because a one-order test passes by luck half the time, and the mutation is now caught. A surviving mutation is evidence the assertion is weak, never evidence the condition is unprovable.

production_measurement.note: The population and the settlement row count are what make pagination mandatory rather than precautionary: a 500-pick chunk can hold far more than PostgREST's default 1000-row page, and a truncated page does not raise -- it silently omits picks, which reads as 'no settlement exists' and makes the caller settle an already-settled pick.

coverage_gap.statement: This runtime proof does NOT exercise the code this lane changed. None of the 18 wired t1-proof suites, and not database-smoke, calls findLatestForPicks or collectLatestSettlementsByPick. What it establishes is that the staging suites are green at this head -- not that the batched PostgREST read behaves as the pure logic assumes.

.range(offset, offset + limit - 1) under the two-key ordering yields disjoint, consecutive pages
coverage_gap.why_it_matters: An under-read is the fail-OPEN direction: an omitted pick reads as 'no settlement exists' and the caller re-settles it. This is the exact class `Require live-DB proof for runtime changes` names (UTV2-519, UTV2-521).
